context.summary: Found by audit run 2 (F-2026-11-23-2). Applied with contract_impact but contracts unchanged: D-imported-event-time-order, D-projections-in-git, D-contract-version-recording, D-post-switch-hand-edits, D-apply-amend-lane (C-event-log v5, C-cli-json v3, C-decision-record v3 texts in T-log-fixes handoff 1), D-cli-json-v3 (T-reconcile and T-skills handoffs) and D-placeholder-task-fields (TaskUpdated). Examples of drift: C-event-log §8 says registry.yaml and state.json are committed, but they are git-ignored; C-cli-json lacks reconcile, contract version, spine approve, project --check and the action InboxItem. Agents read contracts, so they work from stale rules.

options.tradeoff: `decision apply` and `reconcile` hold a contract_impact decision until each named contract has a ContractVersioned by that decision; the inbox shows "version C-x for D-y" to the orchestrator. Applied then means the contract says it. The seven applied ones need a one-off catch-up.
Keep apply as is, and add a check rule or inbox action (contract-behind) for decided contract_impact decisions with no ContractVersioned. Detects drift without changing apply.
No change. Contracts are updated whenever the orchestrator gets to it; nothing tracks the gap.

data.question: Seven decisions with contract_impact are marked applied (applied_on 2026-11-20), but no ContractVersioned event exists and no contract file has changed since a8af023. The frozen C-event-log (v4), C-cli-json (v2) and C-decision-record (v2) no longer describe merged code. Should applying a decision with contract_impact require the contract-change protocol to have run first?
data.title: Hold a contract-changing decision's apply until its contract is versioned
